notes: Read all 51 source lines line by line before editing. The web hook is a mount-once side effect with three moving parts: (A) SSE 'alert' subscription -> invalidate the unread-count query (a fast-refresh optimization), (B) compute a '(N) '/'(99+) ' prefix from count + tab_badge_enabled and write it into document.title via titleStore.setBasePrefix, and (C) clear the prefix on unmount. Part (B)'s count->prefix math is the portable core and ports 1:1. Parts (A) and the document.title write are structurally browser-only and absent from the native parity manifest (contract rules 4,5,7), so the native port DERIVES and RETURNS the badge (native pattern: turn a global-mutation side effect into consumable state, cf. useChartPalette returning a value; explicit-unavailable status, cf. useNotificationListener / useAchievementUnlocks) instead of mutating a non-existent global title bar. Return type widened from `void` to `UseTitleBadgeResult`; safe because no native consumer imports useTitleBadge yet (grep: 0 matches under apps/native).

L1 `import { useEffect } from 'react'` REMOVED: the native port is pure derived state, so none of the three web useEffects survive as effects — (A) the SSE effect is unavailable, (B) the title-write becomes a synchronous derivation, and (C) the unmount-clear is satisfied implicitly (a returned value disappears on unmount, leaving no global dirty). L2 `import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'` REMOVED: `qc` (web L22) was only used by the dropped SSE invalidation (web L31).

L3 `import { notificationKeys, useUnreadCount } from '@/api/hooks/useNotifications'` -> `import { useUnreadCount } from '../api/hooks/useNotifications'`: useUnreadCount is the native parity TanStack Query hook (api/hooks/useNotifications.ts L986-994) whose `select: data => data?.count ?? 0` already yields a number, matching the web hook's `{ data: count = 0 }` contract. `notificationKeys` is dropped because its only use (web L31 `notificationKeys.unreadCount`) was inside the dropped SSE invalidation; notificationKeys.unreadCount still exists in the native hook (L444) for the poll-invalidation paths.

L4 `import { useSettings } from '@/hooks/useSettings'` -> `import { useSettings } from '../api/hooks/useSettings'`: the web app-level @/hooks/useSettings (returns `{ settings }`) has no native parity port, but its `tab_badge_enabled` field lives on `AppSettings` (api/hooks/useSettings.ts L84) returned by the canonical native settings query hook — the exact same settings-access substitution useChartPalette.ts already established (`const { data } = useSettings(); ... data?.chart_palette`).

L5 `import { sseManager } from '@/lib/sseManager'` REMOVED: the browser EventSource singleton's generic 'alert' channel (sseManager.ts: `new EventSource('/api/v1/events')` dispatching named 'alert' events) has no ported module on native. The native `api/sseClient.ts` only carries typed `signal_change` envelopes filtered by vehicle/field, so it cannot stand in for a generic alert broadcast. Per the useNotificationListener precedent, no dead SSE subscription is wired; the fast-refresh path is surfaced as explicit-unavailable. L6 `import { setBasePrefix } from '@/lib/titleStore'` REMOVED: React Native has no global document.title; titleStore is the single owner of the one browser tab title bar, a surface that does not exist on native. The badge is returned for a native host to render instead.

L8-20 the file/hook JSDoc (mirrors unread count into document.title as a capped '(N) ' prefix; disappears at zero or when tab_badge_enabled is disabled; SSE 'alert' subscription invalidates the unread-count query for sub-second refresh vs the 30s poll; mount once near the app root) is preserved and restated for native in the file header + hook JSDoc, including why the document.title mirror and SSE fast-path are unavailable and how the count still refreshes via the useUnreadCount 30s poll.

L21 `export function useTitleBadge(): void {` -> `export function useTitleBadge(): UseTitleBadgeResult {`: name preserved verbatim; the `void` return is widened to a derived-badge result object because native has no global title to write — the badge that the web hook pushed into document.title is instead returned (count, enabled, visible, badgeLabel, badgePrefix) plus the explicit titleSyncStatus:'unavailable' + unavailableReason (contract rule 7).

L22 `const qc = useQueryClient()` DROPPED (only used by the unavailable SSE invalidation). L23 `const { data: count = 0 } = useUnreadCount()` preserved VERBATIM — the `= 0` default mirrors the web hook so an unloaded query reads as 0. L24 `const { settings } = useSettings()` -> `const { data: settings } = useSettings()`: the native api hook returns a UseQueryResult (data: AppSettings | undefined) rather than the web app-hook's `{ settings }`, so the destructure targets `data`. L25 `const enabled = settings.tab_badge_enabled !== false` -> `const enabled = settings?.tab_badge_enabled !== false`: optional chaining added because the native query `data` may be undefined while loading; the `!== false` default-ON semantics are preserved exactly (undefined -> enabled, matching the web test 'treats undefined tab_badge_enabled as enabled').

L27-35 EFFECT (A) — the `useEffect` that does `sseManager.subscribe('alert', onAlert)` / `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: notificationKeys.unreadCount })` / `return () => sseManager.unsubscribe('alert', onAlert)` (web L29-35) — is NOT wired on native and is documented in the file header. Intent preserved verbatim in prose: an alert fires -> invalidate the unread-count query so the badge updates within a few hundred ms instead of waiting for the periodic refetch. On native this optimization is unavailable (no ported generic-alert sseManager), but correctness is retained because useUnreadCount's `refetchInterval: INTERVALS.STANDARD` (30s) still refreshes the count — the same behavior the web badge would exhibit with SSE down. Surfaced via titleSyncStatus:'unavailable' / TITLE_BADGE_SYNC_UNAVAILABLE_REASON.

L37-44 EFFECT (B) — `if (!enabled || count === 0) { setBasePrefix(''); return }` then `const display = count > 99 ? '99+' : String(count); setBasePrefix(`(${display}) `)` — is ported as SYNCHRONOUS DERIVED state with byte-faithful logic: `const visible = enabled && count !== 0` (the inverse of the `!enabled || count === 0` early-return guard); `const cappedLabel = count > TITLE_BADGE_MAX ? `${TITLE_BADGE_MAX}+` : String(count)` preserves the web `count > 99 ? '99+' : String(count)` cap (TITLE_BADGE_MAX = 99 named for clarity); `const badgeLabel = visible ? cappedLabel : ''` and `const badgePrefix = visible ? `(${badgeLabel}) ` : ''` reproduce the exact strings web fed to setBasePrefix ('' when hidden, '(N) '/'(99+) ' when shown). Verified against all web test cases: count 0 -> '', count 3 -> '(3) ', count 250 -> '(99+) ', enabled=false -> '', enabled=undefined+count 1 -> '(1) '.

L46-50 EFFECT (C) — `useEffect(() => () => setBasePrefix(''), [])`, the unmount cleanup that clears the prefix so a hot-reload/remount does not leave a stale badge — is satisfied IMPLICITLY by the return-value model: because the badge is derived and returned (never written to a module-level/global store), unmounting the host component stops rendering the badge and leaves nothing dirty, which is strictly stronger than the web's manual global clear. Documented in the file header. L51 closing brace + L52 trailing newline preserved.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components are imported — only the native parity hooks `../api/hooks/useSettings` and `../api/hooks/useNotifications`. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit); npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
